finding.title: "Require MFA for all users" is not enforced: login hands out a fully privileged token and only sets an advisory need_bind_mfa flag; nothing server-side gates unbound users
finding.evidence: auth.go:133-138 `needBind := sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled` … `s.ok(c, gin.H{"token": token, "user": ..., "need_bind_mfa": needBind})` — the token is issued unconditionally; the flag is data only. middleware.go:14-31 validates nothing but the signature and never looks at MFA state. settings/settings.go:87 `return Security{MFAEnabled: true, MFARequiredAll: false, RecoveryCodeCount: 10, GraceDays: 7}` — grep shows `GraceDays` has zero references in backend/, and grep for MFARequiredAll finds only auth.go:133. The UI label says '强制所有用户启用 MFA' / 'Require MFA for All Users' (i18n security.ts:8) while the tooltip admits users are only 'guided' to enrol.
finding.impact: A user who never binds MFA — or an attacker who obtains such an account's password via authn-3/authn-4/authn-10 — authenticates with one factor and receives a token that passes every authorization check in the admin API, including the endpoints that change security policy (PUT /settings/security) or strip other users' MFA (POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa). Skipping enrolment costs nothing: `curl` against /api/admin/v1/* works; the only consequence is a client-side redirect (Login.tsx:46-48) and a hint paragraph (AccountSecurity.tsx:314-318), bypassed by not using the SPA. RequireAuth (App.tsx:67-72) checks only token presence. The 7-day grace concept implied by GraceDays is unimplemented.
finding.mitigations_checked: the second factor IS enforced for users who have bound it (auth.go:86-108; the ticket branch at auth.go:46-73 cannot be skipped by omitting totp_code — omitting it yields a ticket, never a token); self-service bind/unbind requires a valid TOTP or recovery code (auth.go:236, auth.go:268-277); recovery codes are stored hashed (mfa.go:50); mfaSetup refuses to re-issue over an existing binding (auth.go:206-209).
finding.recommendation: Gate the authenticated group: in AuthMiddleware (or a second middleware) load the user and reject with a dedicated code (e.g. 40302) when `sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled` unless the request targets the enrolment/password endpoints; or issue a scoped enrolment-only token until binding completes. Implement or remove `grace_days`, and stop naming an advisory prompt 'require/强制'.

reason:
VERDICT: confirmed as filed; every quoted line was opened and matched verbatim, and the attack chain survives every mitigation I could find in the flow. No line correction needed (the primary citation, backend/internal/admin/auth.go:133, is exact).

LINE-BY-LINE EVIDENCE AUDIT:
1) auth.go:133-138 — exact match: `133: needBind := sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled` followed by `s.ok(c, gin.H{"token": token, "user": gin.H{...}, "need_bind_mfa": needBind})` (lines 134-138). `auth.Issue(s.secret, u.ID, u.Username)` is called at line 125 — i.e. the signed token is created and `last_login_at` + the `login` op-audit are written (131-132) BEFORE needBind is even computed, and nothing about needBind is fed into the token. auth/jwt.go:11-27 shows the Claims struct is only {uid, uname, exp, iat, iss} — there is no amr/mfa claim to gate on, and 24h expiry (jwt.go:21). So the flag is provably response-body data only.
2) admin/middleware.go — read end-to-end (33 lines total). AuthMiddleware does exactly three things: require `Bearer ` prefix (17-21), `auth.Parse(s.secret, token)` signature/expiry (23-28), `c.Set("operator"/"userID")` (29-30). No DB lookup of AdminUser, no MFA state, no grace-period check. The citation 'middleware.go:14-31' is accurate (31 is `c.Next()`).
3) grep for `MFAEnabled|mfa_enabled|MFABoundAt` across backend/ returns hits only in auth.go (login/prompt/me/status/bind/unbind), users.go (list/unbind), model.go, settings.go — i.e. the sole server-side consumer of MFA state is auth.go:86 (which requires `u.MFAEnabled`) and auth.go:133 (which only computes the advisory flag). grep for `MFARequiredAll|mfa_required_for_all|GraceDays|grace_days` across backend/ returns exactly 4 hits: auth.go:133, and settings.go:81/83/87 (struct field + default). `GraceDays` is declared and defaulted to 7 but never read anywhere — the 'enforcement grace period' advertised in the UI (frontend/src/pages/settings/Security.tsx:113-115, form field `name="grace_days"`) is dead config.
4) Only ONE gin.HandlerFunc exists in the whole admin package (grep `gin.HandlerFunc` → middleware.go:14). routes.go read end-to-end: every protected route is gated by `s.AuthMiddleware()` alone (routes.go:43-148); there is no second middleware, no role check, no MFA check. So the finding's 'nothing server-side gates unbound users' is literally true.
5) Frontend claims all verified: Login.tsx:44-51 stores the token first (`45: setAuth(res.token, res.user)`) and only then `46: if (res.need_bind_mfa) { 47: message.warning(...); 48: navigate('/account/security', {replace:true}) }` — a soft redirect inside an already-authenticated session. store/auth.ts:33 `export const isLoggedIn = () => Boolean(useAuthStore.getState().token)` and App.tsx:67-72 RequireAuth → `if (!isLoggedIn()) return <Navigate to="/login" .../>`: token presence only, and no route anywhere checks `user.mfa_enabled`. AccountSecurity.tsx:313-318 is the `{me && !bound && step === 0 && ... t('acctSec.forcedTip')}` hint paragraph. i18n labels verified: zh-CN/pages/security.ts:8 `'security.mfaRequired': '强制所有用户启用 MFA'` and en-US/pages/security.ts:8 `'Require MFA for All Users'`, with en-US:9 `'security.mfaRequiredTooltip': 'When on, users without MFA are guided through enrollment after login'` — the product itself admits the control is advisory while naming it 'require/强制'.
6) The 'mitigations_checked' claims are also accurate, so the finding is not overclaiming: auth.go:86-108 does enforce 2FA for bound users; the ticket branch cannot be bypassed (auth.go:66-70 → `ok2` false → 40103, and PopLoginTicket at :47 makes tickets single-use, uid-bound at :52-55); self-service mfaEnable requires a valid TOTP (auth.go:236) and mfaDisable a valid TOTP or consumed recovery code (auth.go:268-277); recovery codes are SHA-256 hashed (mfa.go:50, compared at mfa.go:63-75).

WHY IT IS STILL A REAL BYPASS (the 'attacker already has the privilege?' test fails in the finding's favour): the privilege being withheld by this control is the second factor. For a user who HAS bound MFA, a password alone yields `{mfa_required, mfa_token}` (auth.go:87-91) and never a token. For a user who has NOT bound MFA, the identical password alone yields a full 24h admin token. That differential is the entire value of the `mfa_required_for_all` toggle, and it is not implemented server-side.
Two corroborating facts make the gap materially worse than 'defence-in-depth hygiene', and are why I keep high rather than downgrade to medium:
(a) There is no user-creation endpoint at all (routes.go:133-135 exposes only GET /users, POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa, POST /users/:id/unlock); the only admin account is the bootstrap user created at cmd/server/main.go:164-184 — `179: u := model.AdminUser{Username: cfg.AdminUser, PasswordHash: string(hash)}` — which leaves MFAEnabled at its Go zero-value false. So in the default single-admin deployment, switching on 'Require MFA for All Users' changes literally nothing: the sole operator account stays unbound and keeps logging in with one factor while the console displays the policy as enforced. The advertised control is non-functional by construction unless that same human volunteers to enrol.
(b) The single-factor token is a full-superuser token, so the bypass converts a password leak into policy destruction rather than just data access: PUT /settings/security is saveSecurity (admin/settings.go:115-128), which persists attacker-supplied JSON with zero validation, and login re-reads it per request (`43: sec := s.securitySettings()` → server.go:52-56 LoadKV). Setting `mfa_enabled:false` therefore strips the second factor from every already-bound admin on their next login (auth.go:86 short-circuits on sec.MFAEnabled), and `POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa` (routes.go:134 → users.go:37-52) force-clears another user's `mfa_secret`/`mfa_enabled`/`recovery_codes_json` with no TOTP, no password re-entry and no confirmation — only an audit row (users.go:50). Combined with GET /backups/:id/download and the API-key CRUD at routes.go:128-131 / provider key management, one password-only token is total console compromise plus durable MFA removal for the legitimate operator.

CAVEATS / PRECISION NOTES (do not change the verdict): (i) The condition is `MFAEnabled && MFARequiredAll` — the bypass only bites when an operator has actually enabled the toggle; the shipped default is false (settings.go:87), which the finding states and does not misrepresent. (ii) docs/api-contract.md:44 (`密码正确但未绑定 MFA → data = {"token": "...", ..., "need_bind_mfa": true}`) shows the token-with-flag response IS the documented contract, and the tooltip honestly says 'guided'. So this is a security-design/labelling defect (a control named 'require' that is enforced only client-side, plus dead `grace_days` config implying a server-side enforcement window) rather than code contradicting its own spec — worth stating in the report but it is not a mitigation: no server-side state or check exists, and the SPA is optional for an attacker. (iii) The finding's cross-references to authn-3/authn-4/authn-10 are plausible credential-acquisition preconditions; the bypass does not depend on them being valid, since the default password path (main.go:170-173, `admin123`) and an unenrolled operator are enough. (iv) Minor wording: 'fully privileged' is accurate only because the model has no roles/permissions at all — every valid JWT is superuser; the finding does not claim otherwise. (v) There is no rate limiting on POST /auth/login (grep: the quota.RateLimiter/RedisLimiter is wired only into the gateway at cmd/server/main.go:63-67 and internal/gateway/gateway.go:40); the only brake is the 5-failure/15-minute lockout in onMFAFail (auth.go:114-122), which also counts wrong passwords (auth.go:77) — this limits online guessing but is no mitigation for phished, reused, or default passwords, which is precisely what MFA is meant to cover.
exploit_sketch:
Precondition: an admin account with `mfa_enabled = false` — which is the state of the ONLY admin account in a default deployment (bootstrap user at cmd/server/main.go:179 never gets MFA bound, and no user-creation endpoint exists). Operator has set 'Require MFA for All Users' in the console (PUT /api/admin/v1/settings/security with {"mfa_enabled":true,"mfa_required_for_all":true,"recovery_code_count":10,"grace_days":7}), believing all admin access is two-factor.

1) Obtain or guess the admin password (default `admin123` from main.go:172, phishing, reuse, or the credential-stuffing paths in authn-3/authn-4). No SPA, no browser needed:

  TOK=$(curl -sS -X POST http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/auth/login \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r .data.token)

  The response is `code:0` + `data.token` + `data.need_bind_mfa:true` (auth.go:133-138). Because `u.MFAEnabled` is false, the 2FA branch at auth.go:86 is skipped entirely — no `mfa_required` step is ever presented. `$TOK` is a normal HS256 JWT valid for 24h (auth/jwt.go:21).

2) Use it against any admin endpoint. AuthMiddleware (middleware.go:17-30) checks only the signature, so nothing notices the missing second factor:

  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/users          # victim MFA/lock state
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/config/export   # provider keys + all settings; then /backups/<id>/download => full DB dump

3) Kill the control so future logins of genuinely 2FA-enrolled admins are single-factor too (saveSecurity has no validation and login re-reads the KV each time, admin/settings.go:115-128 + auth.go:43):

  curl -sS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"mfa_enabled":false,"mfa_required_for_all":false,"recovery_code_count":10,"grace_days":0}' \
    http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/settings/security

4) Or strip a specific bound user's second factor with no TOTP/password confirmation (users.go:37-52), then log in as them on the next attempt with auth.go:86 now false:

  curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/users/1/unbind-mfa

Only cosmetic consequence of skipping enrolment: the SPA's `navigate('/account/security')` (Login.tsx:48) — never executed by curl. `grace_days` is never read (grep: settings.go:83/87 only), so there is not even a delayed enforcement window to wait out or violate.
recommendation: Enforce server-side, not client-side: in AuthMiddleware (or a second middleware on the authenticated group) load the AdminUser and reject with a dedicated code (e.g. 40302) when `sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled`, allow-listing only /account/mfa/*, /auth/me and /auth/password; alternatively refuse to issue a privileged token at login until binding completes (or add an `amr`/`mfa` claim and a scoped enrolment-only token). Do not let POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa or PUT /settings/security proceed on a session that satisfied only one factor, and require a second-factor proof for those destructive security changes. Either implement `grace_days` (compare `u.MFABoundAt`/`u.CreatedAt` against it and hard-block after expiry) or delete the field, and rename the control away from 'require/强制' while it remains advisory. A must-enrol state would also close the gap where the bootstrap admin (main.go:179, MFAEnabled=false) is the only account.
